extra.reason: Scaffolded @mastra/telegram: package.json (deps @mastra/core peer + @chat-adapter/telegram), tsconfig, tsup, Vitest harness (undici for Bot-API mocking; no AIMock), TelegramProvider ChannelProvider skeleton. Verified: npm install + tsc typecheck + tsup build + 4 vitest tests all green.

Implemented TelegramProvider (implements ChannelProvider: id/getRoutes required + initialize/configure/getInfo/connect/disconnect/listInstallations). connect() returns immediate (validated token via getMe) or deep_link (BotFather); multi-token install store over ChannelsStorage keyed by agent (one bot=one agent) with fields botToken/secretToken/username/webhookUrl. typecheck + 12 tests green; tsup build ok. Files: src/{types,telegram-client,install-store,telegram-provider,index}.ts, test/telegram-provider.test.ts

Per-bot setWebhook lifecycle (url+secret_token+allowed_updates+drop_pending_updates) on connect; deleteWebhook on disconnect; webhook<->polling exclusion (auto→webhook when baseUrl else polling; polling clears webhook first; explicit webhook w/o baseUrl throws). Mounted POST /api/webhooks/telegram/:webhookId with withInit auto-init, constant-time X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token verification (404 unknown / 401 bad secret), then delegates to AgentChannels.handleWebhookEvent (adapter built per install + injected via AgentChannels, mirroring @mastra/slack). typecheck + 17 tests green; build ok. Files: src/{telegram-client,telegram-provider,types,index}.ts, test/telegram-provider.test.ts

setMyCommands: normalizeCommands maps agent capabilities/connect-options -> BotCommand[] (lowercase, strip slash, [a-z0-9_], 1-32 cmd / 1-256 desc, dedup), seeds /start /help /settings by default, best-effort setMyCommands on connect with optional commandScope. Stream binding: resolveTelegramAdapterConfig plumbs streaming (post-and-edit editMessageText chunking, 4096 cap in adapter) + typingStatus (sendChatAction keepalive) onto the AgentChannels telegram adapter entry, both default-on and configurable. typecheck + 24 tests green; build ok. Files: src/{commands,telegram-client,types,install-store,telegram-provider,index}.ts, test/telegram-provider.test.ts

Opt-in AES-256-GCM encryption at rest for botToken/secretToken (src/crypto.ts: scrypt-derived key, per-value random IV, 'enc:v1:' versioned prefix so plaintext/ciphertext coexist and decrypt no-ops on plaintext). TelegramInstallStore takes encryptionKey (provider passes config.encryptionKey ?? MASTRA_ENCRYPTION_KEY); encrypts on write, decrypts transparently on read; no key = plaintext (dev). typecheck + 34 tests green (crypto round-trip + wrong-key + store encrypt-at-rest/plaintext paths); build ok. Files: src/{crypto,install-store,types,telegram-provider}.ts, test/crypto.test.ts, README.md

Live e2e PASSED: real message to @ccmechellybot -> Telegram webhook -> ngrok -> provider route (constant-time secret verified) -> OpenAI agent -> reply delivered. Independently confirmed: ngrok logged webhook POST -> 200 (88ms), user confirmed bot reply. Also validated real getMe against live Bot API. Note: cloudflared quick-tunnel data path was blocked on this network (control conn registers but HTTP never reaches origin); pivoted to ngrok. Server bind must be IPv4 127.0.0.1 on Windows (node-server defaulted to :: IPv6-only).

Added automated happy-path integration test: a real Telegram message update posted to the mounted webhook route (correct secret) routes through handleWebhookEvent to a real Agent backed by @mastra/core's createMockModel, and a reply sendMessage is issued to the sender's chat with the agent's text. Uses waitUntil to deterministically drain the background run. Gate green: typecheck clean, 35 tests pass (was 34), build ok. Also added test/mastra-test-utils.d.ts ambient shim (upstream ships the llm-mock runtime export but not its .d.ts) and fixed missing Agent id in example/telegram-agent.ts.

ChannelConfig passthrough parity DONE. Widened TelegramProviderConfig to forward the curated @mastra/slack subset to AgentChannels: channel-level (handlers, inlineMedia, inlineLinks, state, threadContext, chatOptions, resolveResourceId, waitUntil, resolveWaitUntil) with ??-fallback to any config the agent author pre-set (no clobber); adapter-entry-level (cors, formatError) alongside existing streaming/typingStatus; adapter-construction (logger -> createTelegramAdapter); provider-level onInstall callback fired after connect. 3 new tests assert the subset reaches AgentChannels.channelConfig (by-ref), the no-clobber path, and onInstall. Gate green: typecheck clean, 38 tests (was 35), build ok. README doc of the surface tracked under i2g.5.

toolDisplay exposed in TelegramProviderConfig, forwarded to the adapter entry, defaulting to 'text' (Telegram has no Block Kit, so Slack's 'grouped'/'cards' degrade to fallback text). Test asserts default 'text' + explicit override. VERIFY: npm run typecheck clean, npm test 40 passed (was 38).

Added public methods getInstallation(agentId) (full installation incl. token, null if none), isConfigured() (active install exists), getAdapter(installationId) (live adapter) — mirroring SlackProvider. Test covers before/after connect state. VERIFY: typecheck clean, 41 tests pass (was 40).

Packaging conventions matched to @mastra/slack: license Apache-2.0, engines node>=22.13.0, keywords, repository (mastra-ai/mastra, directory channels/telegram), homepage, bugs, publishConfig public, dev (tsup --watch) script, CHANGELOG.md, dropped private:true, removed redundant module field. DUAL ESM+CJS INTENTIONALLY NOT SHIPPED: @chat-adapter/telegram is strictly ESM-only (exports has only types+import, no require/default), so a CJS bundle's require() of it throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. Verified: shipping index.cjs loads-broken. Correct call = ESM-only (matches the adapter); CJS consumers use dynamic import() (verified working) or require(esm) on Node>=22.12. VERIFY: clean build produces index.js + index.d.ts only; ESM import ok, CJS dynamic import ok; typecheck clean, 41 tests pass.

Added .github/workflows/ci.yml: on push (main/master) + pull_request, runs npm ci -> typecheck -> test -> build on node 22.13.0 (ubuntu). VERIFY: the four commands it runs are the same locally-green gate (typecheck clean, 41 tests, build ok).

Reactions exposed via the  ChannelConfig passthrough (add_reaction/remove_reaction; message_reaction already in allowedUpdates) — forwarded + tested (tools on/off). Inline keyboards are adapter-native; README documents the interactive surface incl. Telegram's 64-byte callback_data cap and that rich elements beyond buttons render as fallback text. VERIFY: tools passthrough asserted in tests (41 pass); README 'Formatting & interactivity' section added.

MarkdownV2 correctness: verified the provider contains NO formatting/escaping code (grep of src/ for parse_mode/markdown/escape = empty) — all rendering is adapter-owned, so double-escaping is structurally impossible. README documents MarkdownV2 context-aware escaping + the { raw } escape hatch for pre-escaped strings. No provider code change needed. VERIFY: grep clean; README 'Formatting & interactivity' documents it.

Polling mode VERIFIED + two real gaps fixed. FINDING: polling DOES start — the adapter's own initialize() (called by the Chat SDK during AgentChannels.initialize) auto-calls startPolling() when runtime mode resolves to 'polling'; core never calls it directly. GAPS FIXED: (1) forward longPolling config to createTelegramAdapter (timeout/limit/retryDelayMs...); (2) disconnect() now calls adapter.stopPolling() (was orphaning the getUpdates loop). New test connects in mode:'polling' and asserts getUpdates is actually called (poll loop live) and that disconnect stops it (no further polls). README documents auto-start + longPolling. VERIFY: typecheck clean, 42 tests pass (was 41), build ok.

Tests + example + docs complete. Tests: 42 passing (unit + happy-path integration + config passthrough + polling). Example: example/telegram-agent.ts (id fixed). Docs: README fully documents connect flow, webhook/polling (+auto-start), commands, streaming, full config surface incl. AgentChannels passthrough, formatting/interactivity (MarkdownV2/{raw}/inline-keyboards/64-byte cap/reactions), ESM-only module format; CHANGELOG.md added. The 'contribute' (publish/PR/email) portion is tracked separately in i2g.7 (gated on user authorization). VERIFY: typecheck clean, 42 tests, build ok.

Validation + research complete (3 agents). TELEGRAM: validated vs real mastra-ai/mastra source — design is contract-correct & closely mirrors channels/slack; 4 fixes applied+verified (edited_channel_post default; dual ESM+CJS build bundling adapter into cjs [corrected my wrong ESM-only call]; route /telegram/events/:webhookId; HKDF crypto). Gate: 44 tests, typecheck+dual-build green. DISCORD: full build-ready spec captured at vault '1. Projects/Mastra/Mastra Channel Wrappers/Mastra Discord Wrapper — Verified Build Spec.md'. Key finding: gateway is CORE's job (set gateway:true, never call startGatewayListener); connect()->oauth variant; two-tier guild-keyed store; /discord/events/:webhookId route with RAW-body Ed25519 (adapter verifies, not wrapper); command registration 200/day/guild; dual-build + reuse HKDF crypto; toolDisplay default 'cards'; no stopGatewayListener (disconnect can't kill gateway window); streaming unverified. No in-flight discord PR (channels/ = slack only).
